claims.claim: Corpus acquisition yielded 456 unique works via cursor pagination and deterministic exact deduplication.
Metadata coverage is 100% for seven core fields, 99.56% for language, 97.37% for DOI, 96.05% for publisher, and 85.09% for abstracts.
The corpus spans 2018–2023; output rose from 1 to a peak of 190 and endpoint CAGR is 185.60%.
All records have the source-supplied article label, which cannot establish the absence of review content.
Briefings in Bioinformatics, Thin Nguyen, and the Chinese Academy of Sciences lead source, author, and institution productivity.
Bradford Zone 1 has 5 sources and 148 documents, versus 120 sources and 151 documents in Zone 3.
Citation counts are right-skewed: mean 59.82, median 24, maximum 1,210, and 22 works uncited.
GraphDTA and Attentive FP are the two most-cited works and their abstracts report strong task performance.
Computer science, artificial intelligence, and machine learning are the three most frequent keywords and increase over time.
The keyword network has 72 displayed nodes, 198 edges, and 7 clusters with a core of computer-science terms.
The reported coupling, citation, coauthorship, cocitation, and institution-network sizes and clusters match the outputs.
Growth and concentration establish that the field is in a hot-topic, nascent phase.
Corpus recency explains the uncited share.
Richer coupling and cocitation maps establish shared intellectual foundations.
The report identifies single-source, retrieval-date, citation-window, metadata, network-parameter, and productivity-quality limitations.
Corpus acquisition yielded 456 unique works via cursor pagination and exact deduplication.
Metadata completeness was assessed for ten fields.
The stated field-specific metadata coverage values are correct.
The corpus spans 2018–2023, grows from 1 to 190 works, and has CAGR 185.6%.
The trajectory is hyper-exponential.
The leading source, author, and institution are Briefings in Bioinformatics, Thin Nguyen, and the Chinese Academy of Sciences.
Bradford-zone counts and the main citation statistics and top-cited works are correct.
The coauthorship network has 60 displayed nodes, 127 edges, and 10 communities, with Hou, Cao, and Hsieh prominent.
The institution network has 71 displayed nodes, 138 edges, and 10 communities, led by the two Chinese Academy institutions.
Collaboration is strongly intra-national and largely bounded within China.
The keyword network has 72 displayed nodes, 198 edges, and 7 communities led by computer-science terms.
Drug discovery, bioinformatics, and chemistry occupy a biomedical-application periphery around a computational core.
Bibliographic coupling delineates four substantive intellectual streams.
Cocitation confirms a foundation anchored by seminal GNN and molecular-featurization papers.
The research front is diversifying into geometry-enhanced, self-supervised, and interpretable architectures.
Association-strength normalization, Louvain clustering, deterministic layouts, and edge reduction were used.
Single-source, citation-window, document-type, abstract-missingness, and network-parameter caveats are acknowledged.

rationale: A covers the major evidence with careful caveats and few unsupported interpretations. B reproduces much of the descriptive evidence but repeatedly converts layouts and rankings into unsupported claims about national boundedness, intellectual streams, thematic peripheries, and emerging architectures.

The five network sizes and cluster counts match the canonical outputs.
The principal keyword trajectories are reported correctly.

The mean-to-median citation ratio shows foundational methodologies concentrate impact.

rationale: A is the more evidence-bounded synthesis: it covers all central results, flags the anomalous top-cited record, and clearly limits interpretation. B is expansive but repeatedly promotes descriptive clusters and trends into unsupported maturity, impact, translational-stage, and intellectual-centrality claims.
